title: Path to Greatness: Treasure Hunt

prize.note: 302,608,794 litoshis. The pot is topped up by the public: the site invites donations straight into the prize address, which is why there are 8 incoming transactions. LTC was $54.17 when I read the price on 2026-09-12; the repository snapshot price of $54 is used here.

target_format: Litecoin WIF, version byte 0xB0 so the string starts with T (compressed) or 6 (uncompressed), encrypted with AES-256-CBC under a 32-byte super_key and the IV goodluck_havefun; the address is P2PKH version 0x30

derivation.summary: The author published the whole scheme on his own clue image computer_screen.jpg. The 8 clue answers concatenate to 128 ASCII characters, which are four AES-256 keys. The 32-byte super_key is cut into four 8-byte segments, each encrypted separately in AES-256-CBC under its own 16-character IV (an album track title), with the key being two clue answers concatenated. Each segment ciphertext is one block holding 8 useful bytes, so its plaintext must end with a PKCS7 padding of eight 0x08 bytes: that is an exact per-segment oracle with a false positive rate of 2^-64, and it needs nothing from the other six answers. The super_key then decrypts the 64-byte WIF blob, and the WIF gives the address through secp256k1, hash160 and base58check 0x30.
derivation.certified_against: the canonical secp256k1 and hash160 vectors for private key 1 (1BgGZ9tcN4rm9KBzDn7KprQz87SZ26SAMH and 1EHNa6Q4Jz2uvNExL497mE43ikXhwF6kZm), eight keys cross-checked between coincurve and the pure Python ecdsa package, the Litecoin version bytes and WIF encoder cross-checked against a third library, synthetic witnesses on both AES layers with 1,024 neighbouring keys rejected, three control negatives, and the author's own arithmetic (8 answer lengths summing to 128, four 16-character IVs, four 16-byte ciphertexts, a 64-byte WIF blob, base64 canonicity of the 22nd character)

difficulty_note: No compute step is missing. The four segments are independent and each has a perfect test, so one reading of one clue is settled in microseconds. What is missing is two of the eight readings: the writing convention for the 16 characters of clue 6 and what clue 1 asks to be written twice (segment 1), and the string the author drew out of the hidden image of clue 7 (segment 3).

third_party_material: Only the author's own published puzzle files are shipped here: the nine clue images served by p2gtreasure.com, the site banner, and the two lossless carriers Beach.png and Ship.png that his QR codes point at. Not shipped, and not to be added: the game demo p2g_demo.zip (134 MB, Google Drive, the author's own but far over the repository size limits), the album audio embedded in it or published on Spotify and iTunes, any frame or transcript of the 1997 film Titanic that the clue 7 montage is built from, and the audio of the author's YouTube video EojQgdZeTyM. All four are linked by URL instead. The clue poems are quoted in short excerpts only, in clues/author-posts.md.
